newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Syrian vice-president meets Libya's Gaddafi.
newsitem.headline: Syrian vice-president meets Libya's Gaddafi.

text.p: Syrian Vice-President Abdel-Halim Khaddam, on a tour of North African countries to build support for Syria's stand in Middle East peace process, met Libyan leader Muammar Gaddafi on Tuesday night.
The official Libyan news agency JANA, monitored in Tunis, reported on Wednesday that Khaddam and Foreign Minister Farouq al-Shara handed to Gaddafi a message from Syrian President Hafez al-Assad.

It said Assad affirmed in his message Syria's opposition to last month's deal between Israel and the Palestinian Authority on the West Bank town of Hebron. He also called on Arab states to stick to their rights, JANA said.
Khaddam later left Tripoli where he arrived a few hours earlier after a visit to Morocco where he met King Hassan on Monday.
Syria says it would resume negotiations with Israel only after the Jewish state agreed to return the Golan Heights occupied by Israel in 1967.

Israeli government of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu refuses to commit itself to the principle of returning land for peace. Damascus says Israel's previous Labour-led government had committed itself to a complete withdrawal from the Golan.
